title: A GTFS route never runs; its trips do, on the dates their service_id allows

cases.name: Date: Mon 4 June 2007 · Stop: Nye County Airport

steps.title: A route row does not promise a departure
steps.line: Seven CSV files decide which trips can actually leave a stop.
steps.caption: The Demo Transit Authority’s sample feed contains routes even on dates when none of their trips run. To find departures at the selected stop, we must join trips to stops and check each trip’s service against the selected date. The GTFS Schedule reference publishes 11 CSV files; these seven contain the rows needed for that question, counted below each header.
steps.picture: 7 labelled values.

steps.title: Seven tables joined by shared IDs
steps.line: Each line joins two files by the ID column named on it.
steps.caption: Each box is one file, with the columns this explainer uses. Each line joins two files by the column named on it. The marks at a line’s ends say how many rows of the table at that end can match one row at the other end; the list on the right reads them.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 5 labels.

steps.title: A route has no times; its trips do
steps.line: Each row of trips.txt names one route in route_id.
steps.caption: routes.txt gives a route its names, vehicle type, colours and web page, and nothing about when it runs. Each row of trips.txt names one route in route_id, so a route has zero or more trips. The reference defines a route as “a group of trips that are displayed to riders as a single service”.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 6 labels. Marked: ROUTE → TRIP: route_id (each ROUTE has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has exactly one ROUTE); focused: ROUTE: route_id (id), route_short_name (text); TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id). New in this step: 6 labels.

steps.title: A trip’s times are rows of stop_times.txt
steps.line: One row per stop a trip makes, in stop_sequence order.
steps.caption: stop_times.txt joins trips to stops: one row for each stop a trip makes, in stop_sequence order, with its times. AB1 leaves Nye County Airport at 8:00 and reaches Bullfrog at 8:10. A trip listed in frequencies.txt repeats through the day on a headway.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 6 labels. Marked: TRIP → STOP_TIME: trip_id (each TRIP has one or more STOP_TIME, each STOP_TIME has exactly one TRIP); STOP → STOP_TIME: stop_id (each STOP has zero or more STOP_TIME, each STOP_TIME has zero or one STOP); focused: TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); STOP_TIME: trip_id (id), stop_sequence (int), stop_id (id), departure_time (time); and 2 more. New in this step: 6 labels.

steps.title: A trip’s service_id may point into either of two tables
steps.line: calendar.txt sets weekdays; calendar_dates.txt changes single dates.
steps.caption: A trip’s service_id must match a row of calendar.txt, of calendar_dates.txt, or both. calendar.txt sets weekdays between a start and an end date; calendar_dates.txt adds or removes single dates. Here FULLW (7 trips) is in calendar.txt and calendar_dates.txt, and WE (4 trips) is in calendar.txt alone.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 4 labels. Either table: CALENDAR → TRIP: service_id (each CALENDAR has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has zero or one CALENDAR); CALENDAR_DATE → TRIP: service_id (each CALENDAR_DATE has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has zero or more CALENDAR_DATE); focused: TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); CALENDAR: service_id (id), monday (enum), tuesday (enum), wednesday (enum), thursday (enum), friday (enum), saturday (enum), sunday (enum), start_date (date), end_date (date); and 1 more. New in this step: 4 labels.

steps.title: On Monday 4 June 2007, no service runs
steps.line: An exception_type 2 row removes FULLW, overriding the monday column.
steps.caption: Monday 4 June 2007 lies between start_date and end_date for both services. FULLW has monday = 1, but calendar_dates.txt removes it on 20070604 with exception_type 2, which overrides the weekly pattern; WE has monday = 0. So none of the 11 trips runs.
steps.picture: Code, 7 lines; 3 labelled values. Applies on this date: 7: FULLW,20070604,2.

steps.title: The day before, Sunday 3 June 2007, runs all 11 trips
steps.line: One bar per trip, grouped by service_id; every bar runs.
steps.caption: One bar per trip, grouped by service_id and labelled with its route. A trip that runs once spans its first departure to its last arrival; a trip in frequencies.txt spans the hours its vehicles leave the first stop. Grey bars, marked “no service”, do not run that day. On 3 June FULLW and WE run.
steps.picture: Gantt chart: 11 tasks.

steps.title: Monday 4 June 2007 runs none of the 11 trips
steps.line: Eleven FULLW and WE trips stop; each gets a new label and colour.
steps.caption: The same chart, edited for 4 June: each trip that starts or stops running gets a new label and colour, 22 edits in all. Eleven trips with service_id FULLW and WE stop. All 5 routes are still in routes.txt; none has a trip running.
steps.picture: Gantt chart: 14 tasks. New in this step: service); service); service); and 11 more.

steps.title: Nothing leaves Nye County Airport on 4 June
steps.line: The card shows what calendar.txt alone would send; FULLW is removed.
steps.caption: A departure is a stop_times row at the stop that is not its trip’s last. On 4 June no trip runs, so no row counts. The card lists what calendar.txt alone would send from Nye County Airport on a Monday; calendar_dates.txt removes FULLW for the day.
steps.picture: “What calendar.txt alone would send, 4 June”, 1 labelled value.

steps.title: A route has no times; its trips do
steps.line: Each row of trips.txt names one route in route_id.
steps.caption: routes.txt gives a route its names, vehicle type, colours and web page, and nothing about when it runs. Each row of trips.txt names one route in route_id, so a route has zero or more trips. The reference defines a route as “a group of trips that are displayed to riders as a single service”.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 6 labels. Marked: ROUTE → TRIP: route_id (each ROUTE has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has exactly one ROUTE); focused: ROUTE: route_id (id), route_short_name (text); TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id). New in this step: 6 labels.

steps.title: A trip’s times are rows of stop_times.txt
steps.line: One row per stop a trip makes, in stop_sequence order.
steps.caption: stop_times.txt joins trips to stops: one row for each stop a trip makes, in stop_sequence order, with its times. AB1 leaves Nye County Airport at 8:00 and reaches Bullfrog at 8:10. A trip listed in frequencies.txt repeats through the day on a headway.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 6 labels. Marked: TRIP → STOP_TIME: trip_id (each TRIP has one or more STOP_TIME, each STOP_TIME has exactly one TRIP); STOP → STOP_TIME: stop_id (each STOP has zero or more STOP_TIME, each STOP_TIME has zero or one STOP); focused: TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); STOP_TIME: trip_id (id), stop_sequence (int), stop_id (id), departure_time (time); and 2 more. New in this step: 6 labels.

steps.title: A trip’s service_id may point into either of two tables
steps.line: calendar.txt sets weekdays; calendar_dates.txt changes single dates.
steps.caption: A trip’s service_id must match a row of calendar.txt, of calendar_dates.txt, or both. calendar.txt sets weekdays between a start and an end date; calendar_dates.txt adds or removes single dates. Here FULLW (7 trips) is in calendar.txt and calendar_dates.txt, and WE (4 trips) is in calendar.txt alone.
steps.picture: ER diagram: 7 entities, 6 relationships; 4 labels. Either table: CALENDAR → TRIP: service_id (each CALENDAR has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has zero or one CALENDAR); CALENDAR_DATE → TRIP: service_id (each CALENDAR_DATE has zero or more TRIP, each TRIP has zero or more CALENDAR_DATE); focused: TRIP: trip_id (id), route_id (id), service_id (id); CALENDAR: service_id (id), monday (enum), tuesday (enum), wednesday (enum), thursday (enum), friday (enum), saturday (enum), sunday (enum), start_date (date), end_date (date); and 1 more. New in this step: 4 labels.

steps.title: On Saturday 9 June 2007, FULLW and WE run
steps.line: The saturday column decides; no exception row matches this date.
steps.caption: Saturday 9 June 2007 lies between start_date and end_date for both services. FULLW has saturday = 1 and runs; WE has saturday = 1 and runs. So all 11 trips run.

steps.title: The day before, Friday 8 June 2007, runs 7 of the 11 trips
steps.line: One bar per trip, grouped by service_id; grey bars do not run.
steps.caption: One bar per trip, grouped by service_id and labelled with its route. A trip that runs once spans its first departure to its last arrival; a trip in frequencies.txt spans the hours its vehicles leave the first stop. Grey bars, marked “no service”, do not run that day. On 8 June FULLW runs.
steps.picture: Gantt chart: 11 tasks.

steps.title: Saturday 9 June 2007 runs all 11 trips
steps.line: Four WE trips start; each gets a new label and colour.
steps.caption: The same chart, edited for 9 June: each trip that starts or stops running gets a new label and colour, 8 edits in all. Four trips with service_id WE start, on route 50.
steps.picture: Gantt chart: 11 tasks. New in this step: AAMV1, route 50; AAMV2, route 50; AAMV3, route 50; and 1 more.

steps.title: Two frequency trips leave Stagecoach Hotel & Casino on 9 June
steps.line: Headways with exact_times empty: the card gives gaps, not times.
steps.caption: A departure is a stop_times row at the stop that is not its trip’s last. CITY1 and STBA start here, on headways with exact_times empty: operators keep the gap, not a timetable. The reference does not say whether a vehicle leaves at end_time, so the card gives gaps. CITY2 ends here and does not count.
steps.picture: “Leaving Stagecoach Hotel & Casino, 9 June”, 7 labelled values.
